articles.title: Farah Khan bids an emotional goodbye to her triplets as they head to college in three cities: 'If u thought moving ur kid to college was hard.. try doing it 3times'
articles.summary: For filmmaker and choreographer Farah Khan, sending one child off to college would be an emotional milestone. But with her triplets embarking on colle.
articles.body: For filmmaker and choreographer Farah Khan, sending one child off to college would be an emotional milestone. But with her triplets embarking on college journeys across three different cities and campuses, the moment has become an especially bittersweet. Farah recently offered a glimpse into the emotional transition, sharing family pictures and a heartfelt message for her children as they prepare to begin this new chapter of their lives.Sharing a series of pictures on social media, Farah reflected on what it feels like to watch her children leave home and take their first steps toward independence. Her message captured the mix of pride, excitement and emotion that comes with saying goodbye to children as they begin building lives of their own.Farah Khan on three children, three campuses and three goodbyesFarah highlighted how challenging the milestone feels when it happens three times over. With her triplets heading to three different cities and campuses, the family is facing three separate goodbyes.“If u thought moving ur kid to college was hard.. try doing it 3times! 3 cities, 3 campuses..3 goodbyes! 3pieces of my heart ❤️❤️❤️ Jao jee lo apni zindagi.. but remember, all roads lead back to Dad & mom..”Her words reflected the bittersweet reality of watching children grow up and become independent. While encouraging her triplets to embrace their new lives and experiences, Farah also reminded them that home would always be waiting for them.Farah gives husband Shirish Kunder a special mentionThe emotional family post also came with Farah's trademark humour. While sharing pictures from the milestone, she playfully called out her husband, filmmaker Shirish Kunder, for managing to stay out of the family photographs.She wrote, “to @shirishkunder for doing everything except cming in the family pics.. ❤️”The light-hearted remark added a dose of humour to an otherwise emotional post, offering a glimpse into the family's playful dynamic.Farah Khan shares a special message for daughter DivaFarah also included a personal note for her daughter Diva, hinting that the song accompanying the post had a special significance for the two of them.She added, “p.s. - @divakunder u know why i chose this song 😜”The playful sign-off offered another glimpse into the close bond Farah shares with her children, even as they prepare to start an important new chapter away from home.An emotional new chapter for Farah Khan and her familyFor Farah and Shirish, the triplets' move to college marks a significant transition for the family. articles.title: De Petrópolis ao Rock in Rio: Zambelli expande projeto de piano | G1
articles.standfirst: DJ e produtor acumula mais de 5 milhões de reproduções, criou os projetos MA.TA e State of Mind e já se apresentou em eventos no Brasil e na Europa.
articles.summary: DJ e produtor acumula mais de 5 milhões de reproduções, criou os projetos MA.TA e State of Mind e já se apresentou em eventos no Brasil e na Europa.
articles.body:
Natural de Petrópolis , na Região Serrana do Rio, o DJ e produtor musical Zambelli apresentou, nesta sexta-feira (4), no Artist Village do Rock in Rio, o projeto “The Path”, voltado a performances ao vivo no piano. Com mais de 5 milhões de reproduções nas plataformas digitais, apresentações em grandes eventos e projetos autorais como MA.TA e State of Mind.

"O Rock in Rio é um marco para qualquer artista. Mais do que mudar uma carreira da noite para o dia, ele traz confiança e mostra que o trabalho está sendo feito da forma certa", disse.

Ao longo da carreira, o petropolitano construiu uma identidade musical própria e conquistou espaço entre os nomes da nova geração da música eletrônica brasileira.

André Zambelli cresceu em um ambiente fortemente ligado à arte, o que despertou seu interesse pela música ainda na infância. Segundo o artista, uma de suas principais inspirações foi a avó, Yolanda Freyre, reconhecida artista plástica e referência de resistência feminina durante a ditadura no Brasil.

Com formação em música pelo Instituto Politécnico de Coimbra, em Portugal, e pela Escola de Música Villa-Lobos, Zambelli ganhou projeção no início da carreira com a faixa "Go With Me", que alcançou 1 milhão de reproduções no primeiro mês e recebeu apoio de artistas como Alok.

Artista petropolitano no Rock in Rio — Foto: Divulgação

Com apoio de nomes como Maz, Joris Voorn, Ritchie Hawtin e Paco Osuna, Zambelli já se apresentou em clubes como Privilège, D-EDGE e Green Valley. Em 2025, estreou em festivais internacionais no Vulkanik Festival, na Itália.

Com identidade voltada ao progressive house e influências brasileiras, o artista lançou músicas por gravadoras como Braslive/Sony, Controversia/Spinnin, Hub Records/Virgin e Ame Records.

Além da carreira como DJ e produtor, Zambelli criou a MA.TA, iniciativa colaborativa voltada ao fortalecimento da cena musical brasileira e à valorização da house music.

Com o lema de promover pertencimento e acolhimento, o projeto já realizou 16 edições em dois anos, incluindo eventos na D-EDGE Rio e no Tawa Beach Club. Entre os artistas que passaram pela iniciativa estão Albuquerque e Leo Janeiro.

State of Mind aposta em experiências imersivas

Outro projeto idealizado por Zambelli é o State of Mind, criado para promover conexões por meio da música e de experiências em locais de significado especial.

As edições já foram realizadas em cenários como o Palácio de Cristal, em Petrópolis, e o Deserto de Atacama, no Chile, combinando música e vivências imersivas.

Criado em agosto, “The Path” é uma extensão do trabalho artístico de Zambelli e propõe apresentações mais orgânicas e espontâneas ao piano, com repertório formado pelas músicas que mais marcaram sua trajetória.

Em menos de um mês de existência, o projeto chegou ao Rock in Rio e marcou um novo momento na trajetória do artista, com uma proposta de conexão mais íntima entre música, público e performer.

articles.title: Passinho no Rock in Rio: Milton Cunha mostra a mistura de ritmos | G1
articles.standfirst: Milton Cunha mostra mistura de ritmos no festival. Para os dançarinos, a presença no festival consolida a dança como arte e cultura.
articles.summary: Milton Cunha acompanha a chegada do passinho ao Rock in Rio, celebrando a mistura do funk com o rock e a valorização da cultura das comunidades cariocas.
articles.body:
Quem disse que no Rock in Rio só tem espaço para o rock? Milton Cunha mostrou que no meio das guitarras, dos grandes shows e das multidões que chegam cedo para garantir um lugar perto do palco, uma dança típica das comunidades cariocas continua ganhando espaço: o passinho.

Com movimentos rápidos e uma coreografia que mistura diferentes referências, o passinho atravessou as fronteiras do baile funk e chegou à Cidade do Rock. Para quem dança, a presença no festival representa uma forma de mostrar que a dança também é arte e cultura.

A mistura não para por aí. No Rock in Rio, o funk encontra o rock, o samba conversa com o pop e diferentes públicos compartilham o mesmo espaço.

Do funk ao rock: passinho conquista espaço no Rock in Rio — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

A ideia é justamente mostrar que a chamada "atitude rock" pode estar presente em diferentes estilos e comportamentos. Para quem participa do festival, enfrentar a vida de frente, independentemente do problema, também é uma forma de ter atitude.

E enquanto o público dança e acompanha os artistas, há também quem esteja trabalhando para fazer o festival acontecer. São profissionais que passam horas na Cidade do Rock e ajudam a garantir que a festa funcione para quem está do outro lado das grades.

Outra preocupação é com o comportamento do público. Com milhares de pessoas circulando pelo espaço, os trabalhadores reforçam a importância de aproveitar os shows sem deixar de lado a educação e o cuidado com o ambiente.

"A gente pode curtir o show, mas também sendo educado", resume um dos trabalhadores.

Entre shows, dança e trabalho, o Rock in Rio acaba se transformando em um retrato da própria cidade: diferentes histórias, sotaques, ritmos e maneiras de viver reunidos em um mesmo lugar.

articles.title: Sapato perdido no Rock in Rio: Mulher faz apelo por plataforma rosa | G1
articles.standfirst: Giullia Pessanha, de 28 anos, diz que o par estava na mochila do irmão quando a bolsa foi aberta durante um show. Segundo ela, outros objetos foram devolvidos, mas os calçados não foram encontrados.
articles.summary: Giullia Pessanha busca seu sapato perdido no Rock in Rio após mochila ser aberta em show e faz apelo nas redes sociais para recuperar o item de valor sentimental.
articles.body:
O que era para ser apenas um sapato escolhido como parte do look para um show acabou virando uma busca no meio do Rock in Rio. A engenheira DevOps Giullia Pessanha, de 28 anos, conta que seu par de sapatos plataforma rosa-choque desapareceu depois que a mochila em que estava guardado foi aberta durante o show de Lvcas, no palco Supernova, no sábado (5).

Giullia conversou com o g1 e disse que havia deixado o calçado na mochila com o irmão. Segundo ela, a bolsa estava fechada, com o zíper travado pelo botão de segurança.

"Como a mochila abre lateralmente, no formato de uma maleta, ela foi aberta e os objetos que estavam dentro caíram no chão", comentou Giullia, que teve vídeo do apelo viralizado nas redes.

Segundo Giullia, ela procurou o espaço de Achados e Perdidos do festival, mas foi informada que o item não constava no catálogo de objetos que foram entregues no local.

A plataforma tem 16,4 centímetros, é rosa-choque, tamanho 37, com amortecimento no calcanhar e palmilha 3D. Giullia conta que chegou a usá-lo apenas uma vez, em uma festa de aniversário.

"Eu tenho 1,57 m e, sem ele, eu só vejo a nuca de um estranho na minha frente. Pessoa que está com o meu sapato, por favor, me devolva. Pode me mandar pelo correio, devolver para o Rock in Rio, fazer qualquer coisa", pediu.

Mulher procura sapato plataforma que desapareceu durante o Rock in Rio — Foto: Reprodução

Giullia postou um vídeo nas redes sociais, em que conta a saga durante a procura pelo objeto. Ela conta que o irmão só percebeu o que havia acontecido depois do fim do show e que ele voltou ao local, perguntando às pessoas se alguém havia encontrado os objetos.

Segundo a engenheira, dois carregadores de celular e um pacote de biscoito foram devolvidos. Os sapatos, porém, não apareceram.

Giullia disse que pessoas que estavam no local disseram que um casal teria saído carregando os sapatos em direção à área dos estandes, como os da Philco. Ela não conseguiu localizar os dois em meio à multidão.

"Eu só queria meu sapato de volta, porque ele não é só um calçado", disse Giullia em um vídeo publicado nas redes sociais.

Giullia postou um vídeo nas redes sociais, em que conta a saga durante a procura pelo objeto — Foto: Reprodução

Assim que percebeu o desaparecimento do objeto, Giullia começou a procurar o par dentro da Cidade do Rock. Ela informou que passou pelo pessoal do palco Supernova e conversou com seguranças das áreas próximas, inclusive nas imediações do estande da Heineken.

Também procurou o setor de achados e perdidos do festival, próximo à saída.

Segundo ela, foi orientada a consultar uma plataforma por meio de um QR Code, onde ficam registrados os objetos encontrados. No local, recebeu a informação de que uma bota havia sido recolhida minutos antes, mas era preta e correspondia a apenas um dos pés.

Ela também ouviu que pessoas tentaram encontrar os calçados durante o tumulto do show, mas não conseguiu confirmar o que aconteceu porque não estava ao lado do irmão quando a mochila foi aberta. O par continua cadastrado na plataforma de achados e perdidos do Rock in Rio.

Giullia contou ao g1 que o sapato foi comprado com seu primeiro salário — Foto: Acervo pessoal/Giullia

O par tinha um significado especial para Giullia. Ela havia comprado os sapatos poucos meses antes, com o primeiro salário depois de fazer uma mudança de carreira: deixou a área militar e entrou no mercado de tecnologia.

Giullia conta que a ideia era usar o calçado justamente em shows. Antes, ela usava uma bota plataforma, que já estava ficando velha. O novo par, no entanto, não foi comprado especificamente para o Rock in Rio, embora o festival estivesse entre os eventos que ela tinha em mente.

O sapato rosa-choque de Giullia não havia sido localizado até a publicação desta reportagem.

articles.title: Fãs de Elton John vestem looks inspirados no cantor na Cidade do Rock | G1
articles.standfirst: Cantor é a principal atração do Palco Mundo nesta segunda-feira (7).
articles.summary: Cantor é a principal atração do Palco Mundo nesta segunda-feira (7).
articles.body:
A advogada Carol Goldenberg usa look inspirado em Elton John — Foto: Cristina Boeckel/g1 Rio

A cidade do Rock foi tomada por óculos e figurinos que fazem referência à carreira de Elton John , atração principal do Palco Mundo nesta segunda-feira (7). Os looks foram um pedido do próprio artista aos fãs, que entraram no clima para o show.

A advogada Carol Goldenberg veio de São Paulo e, desde cedo, garantiu lugar na grade do palco para ver o ídolo, que aprendeu a amar com a mãe.

"Na minha infância, meus pais sempre ouviram, a minha mãe é muito fã e me passou isso. Desde que me conheço por gente eu escuto Elton John. Fui criando essa paixão e virei super fã ", contou.

Brincos inspirados em Elton John — Foto: Cristina Boeckel/g1 Rio

Carol está emocionada com a possibilidade de ver o último show do artista no Brasil, depois da turnê de despedida do artista.

"Eu estou muito emocionada, a última vez que o vi no Brasil foi em 2017. Eu fiquei muito ansiosa pela turnê de despedida dele, que ele fez no mundo inteiro, cheguei a pensar em ir para fora para ver e era tudo muito caro. Tava esperando vir para a América Latina e não veio. Eu achei que não ia mais vê-lo. Então, quando anunciaram, foi uma emoção gigantesca e fiz de tudo para estar aqui hoje", disse a advogada.

Ela vestia um figurino inspirado no show do artista no Dodger Stadium, em 1975. Outros fãs também vestiam looks inspirados na mesma apresentação.

A designer Giovanna Martim vai se revezar com uma amiga na grade até a hora do show. O amor por Elton John surgiu a partir da própria busca por referências pop.

"Não tenho pais e parentes que curtem, é uma coisa que descobri sozinha. Há alguns anos acompanho e não imaginava poder vê-lo ao vivo", contou.

A designer Giovanna Martim disse que o amor por Elton John surgiu a partir da própria busca por referências pop — Foto: Cristina Boeckel/g1 Rio

A profissional de marketing Alê Moraes também aprendeu a amar as canções de Elton John com a família e customizou os óculos de grau com brilhos rosa. Na roupa, um foguete inspirado na canção "Rocket Man".

"Desde que nasci eu escuto no rádio com a minha mãe e, a partir daí, não parei mais. Veio cada música e, depois veio 'O Rei Leão'. Foi meu primeiro filme no cinema", disse a fã.

Alê Moraes customizou os óculos de grau com brilhos rosa — Foto: Cristina Boeckel/g1 Rio

Marla Marques veio de Salvador para acompanhar o show do cantor no Rock in Rio com um visual que faz referência ao trabalho do artista. Ela começou a conhecer a obra de Elton John a partir das referências feitas a ele por outros artistas. A partir daí, se encantou com o trabalho dele.

Marla Marques veio de Salvador para ver Elton John — Foto: Cristina Boeckel/g1 Rio

articles.title: Daniela Mercury confirma a Mangueira como o lugar onde o Rio é mais baiano ao dar voz ao samba do Carnaval 2027 | G1
articles.body:
Daniela Mercury defende o samba 'Oyá por nós', escolhido pela Mangueira na madrugada de domingo, 6 de setembro, para representar a escola no Carnaval de 2027 — Foto: Célia Santos / Reprodução X Daniela Mercury

♬ Em 1994, no embalo da homenagem prestada pela Mangueira aos Doces Bárbaros no Carnaval daquele ano, Caetano Veloso compôs um samba, “Onde o Rio é mais baiano”, em exaltação à Estação Primeira de Mangueira . O artista deu o samba para Alcione lançar em gravação feita pela cantora com o próprio Caetano para o álbum “Brasil de Oliveira da Silva do Samba” (1994).

Decorridos 32 anos, a Mangueira se confirma mais uma vez o lugar onde a cidade do Rio de Janeiro (RJ) é mais baiana. Na noite de sábado, 5 de setembro, coube a Daniela Mercury interpretar o samba-enredo finalista que, já na madrugada de domingo, 6 de setembro, foi eleito o vencedor da disputa para o Carnaval de 2027, tendo sido escolhido pela comunidade mangueirense para ser cantado pela agremiação verde e rosa no desfile do próximo Carnaval carioca.

O samba se chama “Oyá por nós”, mesmo nome da música composta por Daniela Mercury em parceria com Margareth Menezes e eternizada pelas artistas em gravação incluída no álbum “Canibália” (2009), de Daniela.

Composição de Lequinho, Júnior Fionda, Gabriel Machado, Guilherme Sá, Rodrigo Bandolim e Orlando Ambrósio, o samba-enredo “Oyá por nós” alude ao hit de Daniela. O samba foi composto a partir do enredo “Oyá por nós”, criado pelo carnavalesco Sidnei França em torno de Iansã, orixá feminino também conhecido como Oyá no Candomblé e identificado com os ventos, as tempestades e o poder feminino.

“Estou emocionada. Agradeço a parceria e o convite de Lequinho e Cia para ser a intérprete desse samba-enredo. E agradeço também a toda comunidade da Mangueira por ter abraçado essa música que nos levanta e dá poder. Meu carnaval começou hoje. Oyá por nós”, celebrou Daniela Mercury nas redes sociais.

A presença da cantora no Palácio do Samba, dando voz ao samba vitorioso, foi a confirmação de que a Mangueira é onde o Rio é mais baiano, como sentencia Caetano Veloso em verso do samba de 1994.

articles.title: Mormaço Cultural 2026: Cachês nacionais somam quase R$ 5 milhões | G1
articles.standfirst: O valor mais alto pago por um show é de R$ 800 mil. Este ano, 13 atrações nacionais participam do festival, entre cantores, chefe de cozinha e companhia de dança.
articles.summary: O valor mais alto pago por um show é de R$ 800 mil. Este ano, 13 atrações nacionais participam do festival, entre cantores, chefe de cozinha e companhia de dança.
articles.body:
Atrações nacionais do Festival Mormaço Cultural 2026. — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram/expocanaa2026/cidadenegra/tavaescrito/ferrugem/kevinochris/pysalles/melodyoficial3/filiperet/dennisdj/pmbv

A Prefeitura de Boa Vista deve gastar quase R$ 5 milhões com cachês de artistas nacionais que se apresentam no Festival Mormaço Cultural 2026 , segundo levantamento do g1 com base nos contratos publicados no Diário Oficial do Município (DOM). O valor mais alto pago por um show é de R$ 800 mil . Veja a lista com os valores abaixo .

O evento começa na quarta-feira (9) e segue até 20 de setembro , no Parque do Rio Branco e no Teatro Municipal de Boa Vista. Este ano, 13 atrações nacionais participam do festival, entre cantores, chefe de cozinha e companhia de dança.

A prefeitura foi procurada pelo g1 para comentar sobre os valores das contratações e o valor total do evento, mas respondeu que não conseguiria levantar as informações devido ao feriado de 7 de setembro.

Os valores constam em extratos de termo de contratos publicados pela prefeitura entre 14 de agosto e 4 de setembro. Ao todo, os cachês somam R$ 4.966.000 . O valor é 11,9% maior que o gasto com as atrações nacionais na edição de 2025, que foi de R$ 4.437.000.

O artista mais bem pago da lista neste ano é o DJ Dennis , com cachê de R$ 800 mil. Ele se apresenta no penúltimo dia do evento, em 19 de setembro .

A segunda contratação mais cara é a do cantor Amado Batista , com cachê de R$ 670 mil . O rapper Felipe Ret e o pagodeiro Ferrugem aparecem empatados na terceira posição, com R$ 600 mil cada .

articles.title: Ônibus com estudantes e professores tomba em rodovia no Acre | G1
articles.standfirst: Veículo levava estudantes de Cruzeiro do Sul, Rodrigues Alves e Mâncio Lima e tombou na BR-364, nesta segunda (7). Não há feridos, segundo a Secretaria de Educação.
articles.summary: Veículo levava estudantes de Cruzeiro do Sul, Rodrigues Alves e Mâncio Lima e tombou na BR-364, nesta segunda (7). Não há feridos, segundo a Secretaria de Educação.
articles.body:
Um ônibus com alunos e professores dos municípios de Cruzeiro do Sul , Rodrigues Alves e Mâncio Lima , no interior do Acre, sofreu um acidente na manhã desta segunda-feira (7) na BR-364, no trecho entre Cruzeiro do Sul e Tarauacá. Ninguém ficou gravemente ferido, segundo a Secretaria de Estado de Educação e Cultura (SEE-AC).

Imagens do acidente mostram o veículo tombado na rodovia. A SEE-AC informou em nota que o grupo seguia do interior para a capital Rio Branco a fim de participar da cerimônia de premiação do projeto Estudantes em Movimento, nesta terça-feira (8). (Veja a nota na íntegra abaixo)

O coordenador do Núcleo da SEE-AC, Alcione Benevides, confirmou ao g1 que uma aluna machucou um dos braços no acidente, mas sem gravidades. Os estudantes e professores estão sendo levados para o Hospital do Juruá, em Cruzeiro do Sul, para avaliação médica.

"O núcleo de Cruzeiro do Sul está ajudando com transporte com uma caminhonete e estamos dando todo suporte necessário aos alunos. Os familiares já foram todos comunicados, ficaram tranquilos e foi feito todos os contatos", explicou.

Ônibus escolar tomba em trecho de rodovia entre Cruzeiro do Sul e Tarauacá, no Acre — Foto: Reprodução

Ainda conforme a SEE-AC, no veículo estavam nove estudantes, três professoras e uma representante da SEE das escolas estaduais Indígena Ixubãy Rabui Puyanawa, de Mâncio Lima; Maria Lima de Souza, de Cruzeiro do Sul; e Francisco Braga de Souza, de Rodrigues Alves.

Duas alunas e uma professora são da escola Indígena Ixubãy Rabui Puyanawa.

"Assim que tomou conhecimento da ocorrência, a SEE acionou, tanto suas equipes nos municípios de Tarauacá e Feijó, quanto a Secretaria de Estado de Segurança Pública, para prestar o suporte necessário. Os estudantes e profissionais estão sendo conduzidos de volta a Cruzeiro do Sul", diz parte da nota da SEE-AC.

Ônibus com estudantes tombou na BR-364 a caminho de Rio Branco — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Leia na íntegra a nota da Secretaria de Educação do Acre

O governo do Estado, por meio da Secretaria de Estado de Educação e Cultura (SEE), informa que um ônibus que transportava estudantes e profissionais da Educação para Rio Branco sofreu um acidente na manhã desta segunda-feira, 7, por volta das 9h, no km 89 da rodovia, no trecho entre Cruzeiro do Sul e Tarauacá. Não há registro de feridos.

No veículo estavam nove estudantes, três professoras e uma representante da SEE, das escolas estaduais Indígena Ixubãy Rabui Puyanawa, de Mâncio Lima; Maria Lima de Souza, de Cruzeiro do Sul; e Francisco Braga de Souza, de Rodrigues Alves. O grupo seguia para Rio Branco para participar, nesta terça-feira, 8, da cerimônia de premiação do projeto Estudantes em Movimento.

Assim que tomou conhecimento da ocorrência, a SEE acionou, tanto suas equipes nos municípios de Tarauacá e Feijó, quanto a Secretaria de Estado de Segurança Pública, para prestar o suporte necessário. Os estudantes e profissionais estão sendo conduzidos de volta a Cruzeiro do Sul.

A SEE está acompanhando toda a situação e também prestando a assistência necessária aos envolvidos e seus familiares.

Reginaldo Prates Secretário de Estado de Educação e Cultura

articles.title: Festival reúne jovens para debater preservação ambiental em Rio Branco | G1
articles.standfirst: Sétima edição do Festival Jovens do Futuro ocorreu nesse domingo (6), na Praça Povos da Floresta, no centro da capital, com música, dança, feira e debates.
articles.summary: Sétima edição do Festival Jovens do Futuro ocorreu neste domingo (6), na Praça Povos da Floresta, no centro da capital, com música, dança, feira e debates.
articles.body:
A Praça Povos da Floresta, em Rio Branco , recebeu nesse domingo (6) a 7ª edição do Festival Jovens do Futuro , evento organizado pelo Comitê Chico Mendes que une música, dança, empreendedorismo e debates sobre os extremos climáticos e a preservação da Amazônia.

A programação reuniu pessoas de diferentes idades em uma tarde de atividades culturais e de discussão sobre os desafios ambientais da região.

O festival surgiu em 6 de setembro de 2020 , ainda durante a pandemia, com a primeira edição em formato virtual. Desde então, a proposta é aproximar a juventude acreana de temas relacionados ao meio ambiente e ao futuro da Amazônia.

A escolha da data também está ligada à história de Chico Mendes , seringueiro, sindicalista e ambientalista acreano que se tornou símbolo da luta pela preservação da Amazônia. No documento, escrito em 1988, Chico cita 6 de setembro de 2120 como a data do centenário de uma revolução.

Festival Jovens do Futuro reuniu música, dança e debates sobre clima e preservação da Amazônia em Rio Branco nesse domingo (6) — Foto: Reprodução/Comitê Chico Mendes

De acordo com Angélica Mendes, neta do ambientalista, a carta deixada pelo avô é a inspiração para o festival e representa uma mensagem para as novas gerações.

“Na carta deixada pelo meu avô, ele fala que no dia 6 de setembro de 2120 haveria o centenário de uma revolução. Então, em 6 de setembro de 2020, a gente começou a primeira edição. Desde então, todo ano, a gente tem falado sobre essa carta pra juventude. Uma carta onde ele sonhou, onde mirou que a gente teria um futuro sem a devastação da natureza , sem pessoas que defendem o meio ambiente sendo assassinadas'', explicou.

Ainda segundo Angélica, levar o debate sobre as mudanças no clima para um ambiente de convivência ajuda a aproximar o tema da juventude, sobretudo diante dos efeitos percebidos na região.

“A gente tá vendo esses extremos climáticos, num ano com o El Niño extremo chegando, e a gente já tá vendo sinais da fumaça, a gente já tá vendo a seca. Então cada vez mais a gente precisa sair de casa pra falar sobre clima, pra falar sobre o meio ambiente. E nada melhor do que fazer isso dançando, ouvindo música, vendo vários produtos legais na feira, saindo e vivendo Rio Branco'', ressaltou.

Entre os participantes do evento também estava a professora de canto Mariana Ravena, que foi prestigiar a programação.

Para ela, o encontro também representa uma oportunidade para que jovens conheçam diferentes perspectivas e tenham espaço para falar sobre questões que fazem parte da realidade amazônica.

“Esse é o momento onde a gente reúne esses jovens para falar sobre isso, mas principalmente que eles tenham voz e que eles pesquisem um pouco mais sobre as coisas que estão acontecendo, principalmente porque nós vivemos na Amazônia. A questão agora é a gente manter e preservar esse lugar onde nós já moramos e nós fazemos parte'', completou.

articles.title: Kailash Kher on Samay Raina-Sharon Verma controversy; says people should know how to laugh and make others laugh
articles.summary: Singer Kailash Kher has addressed the controversy surrounding jokes about Bihar and Kashmir on 'India's Got Latent' Season 2. The exchange involved co.
articles.body: Singer Kailash Kher has addressed the controversy surrounding jokes about Bihar and Kashmir on 'India's Got Latent' Season 2. The exchange involved comedian Samay Raina and comedian Sharon Verma. Clips from their interaction have attracted criticism on social media.The discussion has also raised questions about the boundaries of comedy. Kailash Kher has now shared his thoughts on how performers should approach sensitive subjects. However, he did not directly attack either Samay Raina or Sharon Verma.Kailash Kher stresses discipline in creativitySpeaking to ANI, Kailash Kher was asked about comedians using subjects related to Biharis and Kashmiri Pandits for humour. He explained his position by drawing a comparison with music.The singer said creative expression also requires discipline. “Look, if I’ll tell you in terms of music, then music is not just a tune its something that can also make you laugh, its also a form of discipline. So, you should stay in music," he said.Kailash Kher further explained that mistakes in artistic expression could change how the audience interprets it. “If your music tune is not correct, then you may end in making fun of someone," Kailash Kher said.Singer talks about awareness and courtesyKailash Kher then expanded his comments beyond music. He stressed the importance of remaining conscious of one's words and behaviour. “To islie manushye ko chaitanye me rehna chahie, tameez me rehna chahie… or apni apni tameez se sb baat krein, to sbko itna to pta hi hai kaise jeena hai, kese hasna hai or kese hsaana hai, kese kisi ka dil jeetna hai…" (“So, a person should remain conscious and aware, and should maintain basic decency. If everyone speaks with that sense of decency, then everyone knows how to live, how to laugh, how to make others laugh, and how to win someone’s heart.”) he said.“There will be critics, there will be haters, there will be jealous people. Then you will realise that you have come so far," he said.What happened between Samay Raina and Sharon Verma?The controversy followed an exchange between Samay Raina and Sharon Verma during 'India's Got Latent' Season 2. Sharon Verma had previously appeared as a contestant in the show's first season. She returned in the second season as a panellist. The panel also included Orry, Archana Puran Singh and Nishant Suri.During the episode, Samay Raina made a joke about Sharon Verma's Bihari background. The comment referred to stereotypes surrounding people from Bihar moving outside the state for employment. Sharon Verma responded with a joke about Samay Raina's Kashmiri identity. Her remark included a reference to “getting stoned". She also said that she had “at least left her state by choice."The exchange was presented as banter during the episode. Clips later circulated widely on social media. The references to Bihar and Kashmir subsequently became a subject of criticism.Samay Raina and Sharon Verma yet to respondNeither Samay Raina nor Sharon Verma has publicly responded to the criticism surrounding their exchange so far.Meanwhile, Kailash Kher is also set to release his latest romantic single 'Tham Jaa'. articles.summary: Sanjay Dutt found a clever way to sidestep an awkward on-stage moment when Maharashtra Transport Minister Pratap Sarnaik asked him to speak in Marathi.
articles.body: Sanjay Dutt found a clever way to sidestep an awkward on-stage moment when Maharashtra Transport Minister Pratap Sarnaik asked him to speak in Marathi at his Dahi Handi event. Instead of attempting the language, the actor cracked a self-deprecating joke about his time in jail, leaving the audience in splits and setting off a wave of reactions online.Sanjay Dutt says he couldn't learn Marathi in six yearsClips from the Dahi Handi event, now doing rounds on social media, show Sanjay Dutt and Pratap Sarnaik sharing the stage along with other guests. The minister referenced his department's recent order requiring Mumbai's autorickshaw drivers to know basic Marathi, joking, "Aajkal main sab logon ko Marathi sikha raha hoon (These days, I’ve been teaching Marathi to everyone)." He then switched to Marathi and turned the spotlight on Sanjay Dutt, telling the gathering that although the actor speaks in Hindi, everyone present could still follow Marathi.Taking the mic, Sanjay Dutt responded with humour, saying, "Pratap bhai. Main 6 saal jail me raha, Yervada mein. Tab bhi Marathi nahi seekh paaya. Main thoda seekha tha (Pratap bhai, I spent six years in jail at Yerwada. Even then, I couldn’t learn Marathi. I picked up a little bit of it, though)." He then wrapped an arm around the minister, referring to him as an old friend, and added, "Main Pratap bhai ka aabhaari hoon ki mujhe yahan bulaye. Hamara rishta bahut purana hai, 25 saal ho gaye hain (I’m grateful to Pratap bhai for inviting me here. We share a very old relationship; it’s been 25 years)."Sanjay Dutt's projectsOn the work front, Sanjay Dutt last appeared in a cameo in the Arabic film '7 Dogs', starring alongside Salman Khan. articles.title: Surprise new Elizabeth Holmes documentary follows Theranos founder's final weeks before prison
articles.summary: The former CEO granted filmmakers extensive access to a project that was kept largely secret for three years.
articles.body:
Elizabeth Holmes, the disgraced founder of blood-testing startup Theranos, is the subject of a new documentary from comedian Nathan Fielder and filmmaker Lance Oppenheim.

You Can See Everything was unveiled Sunday as a surprise screening at the Telluride Film Festival after being made largely in secret over three years. Filming began 34 days before Holmes was due to report to federal prison. The documentary is set to be released in theaters in October.

Holmes founded Theranos at 19 and became a celebrated Silicon Valley entrepreneur by claiming the company had developed technology capable of performing a wide range of medical tests using a small amount of blood. But the technology did not live up to her claims, and in 2022, Holmes was convicted of defrauding Theranos investors. She is serving a federal prison sentence.

You Can See Everything is co-directed by Fielder, best known for the Comedy Central series Nathan for You , and Oppenheim, who directed the Robert Pattinson film Primetime .

Holmes was looking for someone to document her life as she prepared to report to prison. Fielder, Oppenheim and a small film crew were ultimately given extensive access to Holmes, her partner, Billy Evans, and their two young children, according to the Los Angeles Times .

The documentary's synopsis reads: "Thirty-four days before she's sent to prison, notorious Silicon Valley founder Elizabeth Holmes invites a skeptical film crew to document her every move. What begins as an intimate portrait of an enigmatic felon becomes a mind-bending three-year journey into the abyss."

The teaser trailer shows Holmes and Fielder staring at each other as he questions whether she is being truthful with him. When he asks if she is being "real," Holmes replies that she is "always being real."

Fielder is known for blurring the lines between reality and performance, and early reviews suggest You Can See Everything takes a similarly unconventional approach. Variety called it "just about the furthest thing from a 'pure' documentary you've seen," while the Los Angeles Times said it was "far stranger than a conventional documentary."

TheWrap argued the film "uncovers complex new layers to the Holmes saga," while Deadline 's critic said it was "unlike any I have ever seen in terms of pure access." Vanity Fair said it was "full of unexpected twists and turns and shocking reveals," with Fielder and Oppenheim having "incredible access" to Holmes and Evans.

Holmes founded Theranos in 2003 and served as the company's CEO. Her pitch helped turn her into one of Silicon Valley's most prominent young entrepreneurs. Forbes estimated her net worth at $4.5 billion in 2014, then revised it to $0 in 2016 as Theranos unraveled.

Theranos raised more than $900 million from investors, including media mogul Rupert Murdoch, software billionaire Larry Ellison and the Walton family behind Walmart. The company planned to set up "mini-labs" in Walgreens and Safeway stores, where its small Edison device would provide faster, less invasive blood testing.

Evidence presented at her trial showed that the company's blood-testing technology produced misleading results and that Theranos used conventional laboratory machines for testing that its own technology could not reliably perform.

In 2018, the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) charged Holmes, Theranos and Ramesh "Sunny" Balwani, Holmes's former romantic partner, who served as the company's president and chief operating officer, with raising more than $700 million from investors through what the agency described as a years-long fraud involving false or exaggerated statements about the company's technology, business and financial performance.

Holmes settled the SEC's civil charges without admitting or denying the allegations. She agreed to pay a $500,000 penalty, relinquish voting control of Theranos, return millions of shares and accept a 10-year ban on serving as an officer or director of a public company.

Amanda Seyfried portrayed Holmes in the 2022 Hulu limited series The Dropout , for which she won an Emmy for her performance.

A federal jury convicted Holmes in 2022 of one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud against Theranos investors and three counts of wire fraud against individual investors. The wire transfers involved in those counts totaled more than $140 million, according to the Justice Department .

Holmes was not convicted of defrauding Theranos patients. The jury acquitted her of a patient-related fraud conspiracy charge and three charges involving individual patients. Jurors could not reach verdicts on three additional investor-related charges.

In November 2022, U.S. District Judge Edward Davila sentenced Holmes to 135 months — 11 years and three months — in federal prison, followed by three years of supervision.

Balwani was separately convicted on all 12 criminal charges against him and sentenced to nearly 13 years in federal prison.

Holmes began serving her sentence in May 2023 at a federal prison in Texas. She is currently projected for release in March 2032, according to Federal Bureau of Prisons records.

A federal appeals court rejected her attempt to overturn her conviction in February 2025 and upheld an order requiring Holmes and Balwani to pay $452 million in restitution.

Holmes told People in 2025 that Evans and her children visit her in prison twice a week. "It kills me to put my family through pain the way I do," she said. "But when I look back on my life, and these angels that have come into it, I can get through anything. It makes me want to fight for all of it."

articles.title: PM Narendra Modi's Economic Advisor Sanjeev Sanyal reacts to 'Dhurandhar' being called propaganda film: 'Let a hundred flowers bloom'
articles.summary: 'Dhurandhar' was a big hit at the box office but it was also called ‘propaganda’ tag which sparked a wider conversation about whether cinema should be.
articles.body: 'Dhurandhar' was a big hit at the box office but it was also called ‘propaganda’ tag which sparked a wider conversation about whether cinema should be judged by the political ideas it puts forward. Economist and author Sanjeev Sanyal has now weighed in on the debate, arguing that filmmakers should have the freedom to tell the stories they want to tell and audiences should have an equal choice to accept or reject them.Sanyal, who is a Member of the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister (EAC-PM), shared his views in an interview recently. His book The Revolutionaries is currently being adapted into a series for Prime Video, and the economist believes there should be room for different viewpoints to coexist in popular cinema.Sanyal also opened up about Ranveer Singh-starrer Dhurandhar, revealing that he watched both films in the franchise after hearing positive feedback from people around him. He admitted that several of the actors were unfamiliar to him before he watched the films, but the franchise helped him discover their work. “I did watch those two Dhurandar films and I really loved them,” Sanyal said. “But you can tell that I didn’t really know many of the actors in that! I literally know who they are because of Dhurandhar," he said in an interview with News18.Speaking about the tendency to label films with a particular political outlook as propaganda, Sanyal said he prefers to apply the same principle that was often suggested to him when he disliked a film’s ideology: simply do not watch it. He argued that filmmakers should be allowed to put their ideas before the audience without being prevented from doing so.“My view is, let a hundred flowers bloom.For example, people in the past would make films which I would consider being, ultra-left wing, which was the default till very recently, I was told that if you don’t like it, don’t watch it,” he said.“So my view remains that that’s a pretty good way of thinking about it. If you don’t like Dhurandhar, don’t watch it. If you don’t like Revolutionaries, don’t watch it. My idea is to present my ideas.”His own project, The Revolutionaries, is based on his book of the same name and explores a particular strand of India’s freedom struggle. Explaining why he feels the story lends itself better to a series than a feature film, Sanyal said the focus is not merely on individual revolutionaries, but on the wider armed revolutionary movement that connected them.“There are innumerable books, documentaries, movies made about individual freedom fighters,” Sanyal said. “Point about the armed struggle is that it is not presented as a movement. And that’s the point about my book.”He pointed out that while personalities such as Bhagat Singh, Chandrashekhar Azad, Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose and Rash Behari Bose are well known, their stories are often presented separately. According to Sanyal, this can obscure the ideological and historical links that connected these figures and helped shape a movement that continued for decades.“You will get the impression that these are heroic characters who got up one morning and did something. But there is a thread that links all these people, that there are certain ideas, frameworks, and historical events that link all of these people into a movement that lasted over many decades.”The series format, he explained, also allows the makers to explore this history at greater length rather than compressing a complex movement into a two- or three-hour film. “So you can have another season and another season and so on, depending on how this one pans out,” he said.Sanyal further clarified that The Revolutionaries does not attempt to offer a comprehensive account of the entire Indian freedom movement. Instead, it focuses on the armed revolutionary stream and the people and ideas associated with it.“I recognise that there are many streams of our freedom struggle, and this is about one of them. It’s part of history. It’s true,” he said.The Revolutionaries is set to premiere on Prime Video on September 11.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.body: Singer-composer Adnan Sami has spoken candidly about the shift in his life and career after officially becoming an Indian citizen. He shared his thoughts during a chat with a trade analyst. Here's what the singer has to say.Adnan Sami says, 'Main India ka hogaya'In an interview with Komal Nahta, reflecting on the change citizenship brought, Adnan Sami said, "It was never difficult for me to get work in India when I was a Pakistani citizen. A lot of things changed after I got Indian citizenship. Main India ka ho gaya aur India mera ho gaya."Adnan Sami's path to Indian citizenshipAdnan Sami became a naturalised Indian citizen on January 1, 2016. He had first entered India in March 2001 on a visitor's visa and steadily built a strong career in the country's music scene. His route to citizenship began after his Pakistani passport lapsed in 2015 without renewal, following which he sought legal status in India on humanitarian grounds.The Ministry of Home Affairs granted him citizenship under Section 6(1) of the Citizenship Act, 1955, a provision that allows naturalisation for individuals who have made significant contributions in fields like art and culture.Support from Asha Bhosle and India's music industryIn an earlier interview, Adnan had shared that limited opportunities and support within Pakistan's music industry pushed him to consider a move to India. He also recalled how veteran singer Asha Bhosle's encouragement played a key role in shaping his decision to build a career in the country. He further acknowledged India for welcoming his music and giving him the space to showcase his artistry.A career spanning decadesAdnan Sami began his musical career in the early 1990s and gradually rose to become a well-known figure in Indian music through his albums and Hindi film songs. He gained widespread recognition with his album 'Kabhi To Nazar Milao', which turned out to be a massive hit.Celebrated for his versatility, Adnan Sami has worked across genres, including Indian classical, pop and film music. articles.summary: La actriz sorprende al hablar en dichos términos en el pódcast 'Not Gonna Lie' presentado por Kylie Kelce
articles.body: Sandra Bullock ha hecho una afirmación rotunda respecto a la presencia de extraterrestres en nuestro planeta. Además la actriz está totalmente convencida de lo que dice puesto que asegura haberlo visto con sus propios ojos. Y ha asegurado haber presenciado un avistamiento de varios objetos voladores mientras trabajaba en Saint Martin. La frase de la artista suena con rotundidad. "Hay naves alienígenas volando por el cielo. Las he visto". Es una de las frases más destacadas y llamativas de su presencia activa en el podcast Not Gonna Lie, presentado por Kylie Kelce. Lo que no se atrevía a decir durante tanto tiempo ha logrado expresarlo. Bullock ha reconstruido lo que vio aquella noche. Bullock explicaba que había terminado de rodar y salió con un grupo de personas a tomar algunas cervezas. De repente estaban tumbados sobre la arena mirando al cielo cuando apareció la primera luz. "Pensé que era un satélite", señalaba. Pero empezaron a sucederse una serie de circunstancias. "Pensaba que era un avión, pero se quedó ahí", explicaba. Después apareció una tercera. Y otra más. "Luego había otra y otra. Eran cinco en total", puntualizaba con exactitud. Las cinco luces se quedaron durante unos instantes en el cielo y realizaron un movimiento conjunto. "Se juntaron y luego, de repente, pfft, salieron disparadas así", indicaba acompañando sus palabras con un gesto para mostrar la velocidad con la que desaparecieron.

articles.title: Nathan Fielder’s surprise Elizabeth Holmes documentary debuts at Telluride
articles.summary: A provocative and previously unannounced documentary from comedian Nathan Fielder and director Lance Oppenheim that features an intimate look at Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes and her family premiered Sunday night in a secrecy-shrouded screening at the Telluride Film Festival in Colorado.
articles.body: TELLURIDE, Colo. — A provocative and previously unannounced documentary from comedian Nathan Fielder and director Lance Oppenheim that features an intimate look at Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes and her family premiered Sunday night in a secrecy-shrouded screening at the Telluride Film Festival in Colorado. The movie, “You Can See Everything,” includes footage of Holmes and her romantic partner, Billy Evans, and their two children interacting with Fielder at a rental home in San Diego in the final days before Holmes entered federal prison in 2023. Portions of the documentary in which Fielder is communicating with Holmes off-camera — including in prison in Texas — are re-created with the help of an A-list actress. The actress’s identity becomes a plot point that Fielder asked attendees not to reveal. “I’m struggling to this day to understand exactly what I experienced,” Fielder said during the post-screening Q&A, of living with Holmes and Evans. “I don’t know why they want me there. I’m a weird guy. I don’t get it. That messed with my head.” It has already garnered some rave reviews. The film originated in 2023 when Oppenheim told his friend Fielder, who is best known for his deadpan, socially awkward comedic style on television shows such as “The Rehearsal” and “Nathan for You,” that Holmes and Evans had approached indie studio A24 about having their story documented. Holmes has been the subject of unauthorized media, including documentaries and a fictionalized Hulu series starring Amanda Seyfried. “I thought the story was fully told,” Fielder said. But, “I was personally curious.” Within a few days, A24 facilitated a meeting between the filmmakers and the couple. And 34 days before Holmes entered prison in Texas, Fielder, Oppenheim and a small camera crew embedded with the family. Much of the nearly three-hour documentary shows Fielder grappling with whether to take Holmes’ words to him at face value. “Why would I deceive you?” Holmes asks Fielder. “There’s no reason for me to do that.” Holmes maintains to Fielder that she never lied in the launching of Theranos, the blood-testing company she founded in 2003 at age 19; in 2022, Holmes was convicted of fraud and misleading investors, and sentenced to more than 11 years in prison. The movie depicts the unusual relationship between Holmes and Evans, who admits to posting from Holmes’ official X account as if he was her, and appears to make key business decisions on her behalf. What exactly Holmes knows about Evans’ activities and whether she condones them is a subject of some mystery in the documentary, which suggests parallels to her relationship with Ramesh “Sunny” Balwani, her ex-boyfriend and the former president and chief operating officer of Theranos, who is serving a 12-year prison sentence for wire fraud and conspiracy. In some scenes, Holmes and Evans are seen making calls to prospective partners to launch a “Theranos 2.0” business, which Evans says he plans to build while Holmes is in prison. In other scenes, they walk together on the beach at sunset and whisk eggs for breakfast. There are startling displays of what seem to be private moments, as when, at one point, Evans allows the crew to film him showering fully naked. The footage also shows Holmes grappling with her imminent imprisonment, including when she cries on the phone while learning about what her living conditions will be and asks, “What is an invasive strip search?” During the Q&A, which was conducted by actor Emma Stone, a friend and collaborator of Fielder’s, Fielder said that Holmes and Evans had not yet seen the film, but that the filmmakers were in touch with them. “Billy was trying to exert a lot of control,” Fielder said, of the filmmaking process. “It caused our communication to break down. The challenging thing is he’s still sort of the conduit to her.” It’s not clear why they chose Fielder, but his career does offer some context. Much of his work has poked at the idiosyncrasies and absurdities of modern business, some of it toeing the line between documentary and fiction. He first burst onto the national comedy scene in 2013 with “Nathan for You” on Comedy Central, then making HBO’s “The Rehearsal,” the second season of which features Fielder getting his commercial pilot’s license and flying a Boeing 737. The logistics of the Telluride screening were highly unusual, with the festival keeping the title secret until the last possible moment, and requiring audience members to stow their phones in secure Yondr pouches to prevent their use during the screening and Q&A. As members of the press were filing into the theater, a representative for A24 handed them notebooks and pens. Despite the secrecy, rumors of the project began to percolate at the festival over the weekend, and the line to see the film in the 650-seat Werner Herzog Theater started forming hours before showtime. “For those of you who don’t know who we are and are disappointed, I apologize,” Fielder said, addressing the crowd before the screening began. “But hopefully by the end of this film, you’ll be less disappointed.” While the audience was in the theater watching the movie, A24 dropped the trailer online, and announced that it plans to release the film in October. Shortly after A24 released the trailer, Holmes’ X account shared it, with the words, “I’m always being real.”

articles.title: Snoop Dogg is hiring an international ice cream taster. Yes, it’s a real job.
articles.summary: If your dream job involves traveling the world, eating ice cream and telling Snoop Dogg which flavors are actually worth trying, you might want to clear your schedule.
articles.body: If your dream job involves traveling the world, eating ice cream and telling Snoop Dogg which flavors are actually worth trying, you might want to clear your schedule. Snoop Dogg’s Dr. Bombay ice cream brand is looking for an International Ice Cream Taster, and the three-month gig pays $30,000. Yes, this is a real job. The position, posted by Dr. Bombay/Bosslady Foods, is open to applicants around the world. The person hired will be paid $10,000 per month as an independent contractor, with hiring and payments handled through Deel. And the job description is basically a love letter to ice cream. “Your mission? Taste. Travel. Discover. Report back to Snoop.” What does the job entail? For three months, the lucky hire will travel the world in search of the best and most interesting frozen desserts. Their assignment includes: Discovering unique ice cream and dessert trendsTasting desserts in different cities and culturesFinding emerging flavors before they become mainstreamSharing discoveries with the Dr. Bombay teamCreating social-media content from their adventuresHelping develop new flavors, campaigns and experiences So, yes, you’ll be eating a lot of ice cream. But you’ll also need to know what you’re talking about. The company says it isn’t looking for a traditional, stuffy food critic. Instead, it wants someone who is curious about food, plugged into culture, comfortable on social media and capable of turning a scoop of ice cream into a story. Creators, foodies, marketers, students, entrepreneurs, journalists, chefs and applicants with unconventional backgrounds are all encouraged to apply. You could help choose Snoop’s next flavor There’s a pretty major perk attached to the gig: The person hired will help Snoop Dogg choose his next ice cream flavor. The job comes with a personal connection for the rapper, too. According to the listing, Snoop’s father grew up on a dairy farm in Mississippi and made ice cream by hand. Snoop later created his own family memories around the dessert, including ice cream stops with his son, Cordell Broadus, after practice. Snoop and Cordell eventually brought those memories to life through Dr. Bombay. The brand combines creamy ice cream with sherbet and unexpected flavor combinations, with the company describing its approach as “nostalgia, remixed.” Now, the brand wants someone to help figure out what’s next. How to apply Before you start packing your suitcase, there are a few requirements. Applicants must: Speak EnglishHave a valid passportBe available for the next three months Additional languages are a plus. The position is a three-month independent contractor engagement paying $10,000 per month, for a total of $30,000. You can apply from anywhere in the world. The job will be hired and paid through Deel, which handles the engagement and payments. If you’re wondering whether you’ll have to make a TikTok of yourself eating ice cream in order to get the job, the listing does encourage applicants to submit videos, social links and other application materials. So, if you have a passport, a serious appreciation for ice cream and an opinion about what flavor the world needs next, this could be your chance.

articles.title: R Madhavan doesn't believe in being a cosmetic father for son Vedaant: 'My profession doesn't allow me, but if you ever need me..'
articles.summary: R Madhavan has never presented parenting as a matter of simply being around his son all the time. The actor, who has often spoken about his relationsh.
articles.body: R Madhavan has never presented parenting as a matter of simply being around his son all the time. The actor, who has often spoken about his relationship with Vedaant Madhavan, believes being a good father has more to do with giving a child confidence, values and the freedom to form his own opinions. His approach, in fact, goes beyond the now common idea of spending “quality time” with kids.Madhavan explained why he does not believe in being a “cosmetic father” who tries to be physically present for every event in his child’s life. He recalled telling Vedaant that his own father was not always around either, but was someone he could depend on whenever he needed support. He also questioned the pressure on parents to create “quality time” with their children.“There will be enough time or there will never be enough time to spend with your kids,” Madhavan said on Mashable Middle East YouTube channel, adding that he did not want to take his career lightly simply because of the pressure to spend more time with his son. “Don’t take the career lightly at this point of time. I think this is a very Western concept that I have to spend quality time with the kids.”He added, "So I said, Vedaant, if you expect me to be this cosmetic father who will come to all your school games, that’s not going to be me because I have a profession that does not allow me to do that." He further added, "But if you ever need any help… I will always be on your side,” he added.One of the things Madhavan deliberately did was give Vedaant a voice in the family from a very young age. In a conversation on The SS Podcast, he said he would ask his son for his opinion even when he was only five. “From a very young age, I treated my son Vedaant like an adult. I never mollycoddled him. When Vedaant was five years old, I would ask him for his opinion on what to do. He has grown up knowing that his opinion matters to me. Children will make mistakes, but I don’t want Vedaant to repeat mine.”That trust has also meant accepting honest feedback from his son. Madhavan said Vedaant is “very blunt” about his films and does not praise him merely because he is his father.In his conversation with Radhika Gupta for ACKO’s 100 Year Life Project, Madhavan spoke about some of the values he consciously tried to build in Vedaant.The first was gratitude. He wanted his son to understand that many privileges come from the hard work of other people.“I realised there are two things I needed to tell Vedaant. One is this attitude of gratitude, which is very, very important for them to know: that they are privileged because of somebody else’s work, that has helped get you this.”The second was respect for everyone, irrespective of their position. Madhavan said he taught Vedaant to acknowledge liftmen, guards and drivers politely. He remembered feeling that he had done his job as a parent when a watchman told him that Vedaant always greeted him with “namaste”.The third lesson came from a family Madhavan stayed with during his time in Canada. Impressed by how well-adjusted their children were, he asked the mother about her approach. Her answer stayed with him: “Don’t give your child free time.” Madhavan explained that the idea was not to burden children with endless activities, but to encourage them to stay engaged with things they genuinely enjoy.Vedaant, born in 2005, has gone on to build a career in competitive swimming and has represented India at national and international events. But Madhavan has also been careful not to let his son confuse his father’s fame with his own achievements.Speaking to Behindwoods TV, he pointed out that there are swimmers in India who are better than Vedaant but receive less attention because they are not the son of a famous actor.“Stardom is a very dangerous thing, my friend. You got it at a very young age. Learn how to handle it because it comes and goes, and mental peace shouldn’t be affected.”For Madhavan, that may be the larger point of parenting — a child does not just need attention. He needs the confidence to think, the discipline to work, the humility to respect others and a parent who remains a steady source of support when things do not go as planned.Vedaant is brutally honest about his father’s filmsMadhavan has also spoken about how Vedaant reacts to his films. Rather than automatically praising his father because he is a star, Vedaant gives him an honest opinion. Madhavan has described his son as “very raw and blunt” when it comes to his work. If he likes a film, he praises it openly, but his reactions are not simply based on the fact that Madhavan is his father.One moment Madhavan remembered particularly fondly came after Vedaant watched Vikram Vedha. His son hugged him after seeing the film, giving Madhavan a personal response that meant more than a routine compliment. It showed the actor how his work was being viewed by his son, who had grown up watching his career from close quarters.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: OJ Simpson jokes about ‘bloody Bronco,’ boasts of its ‘great escapability’ in disturbing resurfaced video
articles.summary: Resurfaced video from O.J. Simpson's prank show "Juiced" captures him joking about a "bloody Bronco" and boasting about its "great escapability."
articles.body: O.J. Simpson turned one of the most infamous moments of his life into a punchline. Years after the fallen football star and Hollywood actor was acquitted of the murders of his ex-wife and her friend, Simpson was caught on camera joking about a "bloody Bronco" and boasting about the vehicle’s "great escapability" — video that has now resurfaced decades later. The moments were captured while Simpson filmed his hidden-camera prank show, "Juiced," in an attempt at a comeback. Simpson’s little-remembered project, which he described as his "own version of 'Punk’d,'" is the subject of a new Investigation Discovery docuseries, "O.J. Unseen: Exploitation of Evil." NICOLE BROWN SIMPSON TOLD FORMER LOVER SHE'D 'RATHER DIE' THAN RETURN TO O.J. SIMPSON BEFORE HER MURDER Simpson faced repeated allegations of domestic violence involving Nicole Brown Simpson. He pleaded no contest to a charge of spousal battery against her in 1989. "O.J. was a malignant narcissist and megalomaniac who thought he could get away with anything — that’s what doing [this docuseries] showed me," filmmaker Rebecca Halpern told Fox News Digital. "O.J. insisted on having a beer in his hand for virtually the entire production, and loose lips sink ships. And there are many scenes in the show where O.J. just starts to blather on about the case. Nobody prompted him to tell a shopper on a used car lot that a white Bronco has ‘great escapability’ and if you do something bad, it can get you out of trouble." WATCH: O.J. SIMPSON DEAD AFTER CANCER BATTLE AT 76 In a scene from the docuseries, which premieres Sept. 7, Simpson pretends to sell a white Bronco at a used car lot, where he boasts about making the car famous. The Bronco appears to have a bullet hole in it. "It was good for me," Simpson tells a prospective buyer. "Got me out of harm’s way." When another customer jokes about whether there is "a dead body inside," Simpson replies, "Yeah, well, hopefully there’s no bodies in this thing." He also tells two other shoppers, "It’s a Bronco, a car that I personally made famous." "This is the best deal we got on the lot," he tells another. "It has escapability, that’s the main thing. I mean, if you ever get into some trouble and you gotta get away, it has escapability. ... I like that word, escapability. ... They weren’t going to let me keep mine." When customers realize they are being filmed for the hidden-camera prank, some laugh, shake Simpson’s hand or embrace him. At one point, he autographs the Bronco. "This is a Bronco signed by O.J. Simpson," he says. "With an authentic bullet hole in it. It’s signed by me, which gives it some kind of extra value." GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE "I wasn’t trying to escape, despite what anybody might tell you. No, that’s the God’s truth. That’s why they never brought the Bronco ride up in any of my trials," Simpson said. "Just take a look around. All you have to do is wash it up." Simpson and Brown married in 1985. They had two children, Sydney and Justin, and divorced in 1992. Two years later, Brown and her friend Ronald Goldman were found stabbed to death outside her Los Angeles home. Investigators quickly focused on Simpson, leading to a slow-speed chase in a white Bronco that aired live on national television. Following the "Trial of the Century," he was acquitted of murder. Simpson was later found liable for the deaths in a separate civil case and served nearly nine years in prison after he was convicted of armed robbery and other charges in an unrelated Las Vegas case. Halpern said Simpson "demonstrated such a complete and total lack of any decency" while discussing his case during filming. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS "He was so desperate for a comeback, to prove to the world that he was still this beloved figure, that he was willing to make jokes at his dead ex-wife’s expense," Halpern said. "And then, on top of that, to shock innocent victims, many of whom were female in these pranks. If that doesn’t say it all, I don’t know what does." "There is [also] a scene at a fast-food restaurant where O.J. begins to fat shame women who are at the drive-thru," Halpern said. articles.title: Bipasha Basu says muscular women weren't acceptable as actresses when she started out, months after Mrunal Thakur's comment on her muscles from an old interview went viral

articles.body: Bipasha Basu has often been associated with her athletic physique, but her fitness journey also played a role in challenging the beauty standards that dominated Bollywood in the early 2000s. At a time when female actors were largely expected to have petite frames and delicate features, Bipasha stood apart with her tall, muscular build and dusky complexion. Now, the actor has reflected on how she believes she helped change the conversation around women and fitness in the industry.Her comments come after an old video of Mrunal Thakur resurfaced online, in which she appeared to take a dig at Bipasha’s muscular physique. The clip triggered a wider debate about women’s bodies and health, while Mrunal subsequently faced criticism over her remarks.In an interview with Elle India, Bipasha recalled how different the prevailing beauty standards were when she entered Bollywood. She pointed out that female actors were often petite, fair and known for delicate features, while her athletic appearance made her stand out.Bipasha also acknowledged that women with a muscular physique were not particularly accepted as actresses at the time. However, she believes her appearance helped pave the way for a different kind of representation of female fitness.“I don’t think women with more muscle tone were very acceptable as actresses. But I think I started the trend, and I started preaching ‘love yourself’ to everyone because I realised it’s not just about looking good. It’s more intrinsic. You need to be healthy.”According to Bipasha, the shift encouraged more women to exercise and think about fitness as a means of staying healthy rather than simply achieving a particular appearance. However, she remains unsure whether the focus on fitness today always comes from the right place, questioning whether people exercise for their health or primarily to look good.The actor also addressed another pressure that women in the entertainment industry frequently face — ageing. Bipasha said she has no intention of allowing societal expectations to dictate how she should look as she gets older.“Ageing is like the biggest sin that you can commit. I believe that I like myself more, the person that I am today, much more than what I used to be in my twenties. What other people are doing, it’s their call. I don’t judge that. But for me, I’m never going to fall into the pressure of wanting to look younger than what I am. I’m very happy with the way I am growing older, and I’m very proud of my age.”Meanwhile, the discussion around Bipasha’s physique resurfaced in connection with an old comment made by Mrunal, dating back to her television days. In the video, Mrunal was seen chatting with her Kumkum Bhagya co-star Arjit Taneja as they discussed the kind of physique one might prefer in a partner.While responding to Arjit, Mrunal brought up Bipasha and said, “Do you want to marry a girl who is manly with muscles? Go marry Bipasha. Listen, I am far better than Bipasha, ok.”The old clip eventually went viral on social media, leading to significant backlash against Mrunal. The actor later apologised for the comment on social media.While the resurfaced video reignited criticism surrounding Mrunal, Bipasha’s recent comments offer a broader perspective on the very beauty standards that once made her muscular physique stand out in Bollywood. articles.title: King Charles clears up confusion over Harry and Meghan's U.K. return with letter confirming their royal roles
articles.summary: The letter has been sent to senior officials in the U.K. government.
articles.body:
King Charles has confirmed Prince Harry and Meghan Markle will remain non-working royals after moving back to live in the U.K.

Under the monarch's guidance, a letter was sent to 'senior stakeholders' in the U.K. government, military and those who represent the British royal family, confirming that Harry and Meghan remain private citizens and will not be able to use the "HRH" titles of His and Her Royal Highness.

According to U.K. news agency the Press Association, the letter reads, "Following the decision by the Duke and Duchess of Sussex to relocate to the U.K., we have received a number of requests for guidance. To help avoid doubt or confusion, the King has directed that the following information be shared.

"It is well known that in January 2020 the Duke and Duchess stepped down from undertaking representative duties on behalf of the Sovereign, and are no longer working members of the Royal Family.

"This position, distinct from the state and royal duties undertaken by the working Royal Family, and with the personal latitude it brings the couple in respect of financial independence and protection of their privacy as they would wish, will continue to be fully respected."

The letter, circulated by the King's most senior official, the Lord Chamberlain, stressed that "there is no change to the current status of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex." It added that the couple's charitable work is a "personal matter for them both and undertaken in their private capacity" and clarified that "In short, their position is akin to private citizens with commercial and charitable interests."

Harry and Meghan returned to Britain with their two children last month, more than six years after moving to the U.S.

They are believed to have flown into the U.K. privately from California, according to the BBC. Their children, Prince Archie, 7, and Princess Lilibet, 5, are set to begin school in Britain this month. AP reported on Aug. 19 that they had already been enrolled, citing a person close to the Duke and Duchess of Sussex who was not authorized to speak publicly.

King Charles III, who was diagnosed with an unspecified form of cancer in 2024, learned about the Sussexes' plans last month. The BBC said it understood that he "welcomes the opportunity to see more of the Sussex family in a private and personal capacity."

Where will Harry and Meghan live in the U.K.?

The family is expected to settle in a privately owned home outside London rather than a royal property.

The Sussexes also intend to keep their home in Montecito, California, and a vacation property in Portugal. Harry and Meghan do not plan to return to being working members of the royal family.

Why have Harry and Meghan moved back to the U.K.?

The move comes as Harry has sought to repair his relationship with his family, particularly his father, Charles.

After losing a legal challenge over his security arrangements in Britain last year, Harry told the BBC that he no longer wanted the family dispute to continue. "I would love reconciliation with my family," he said at the time.

The family was in Britain as recently as July. During that trip, Harry, Meghan and their children spent time with Charles at his Highgrove estate. The visit also reunited Charles with Archie and Lilibet for the first time since Queen Elizabeth II's platinum jubilee celebrations in 2022.

Relations between Harry and his older brother, Prince William, remain strained. Reuters reported that the brothers are still barely speaking.

Peter Hunt, a former BBC royal correspondent, said the surprise return is likely to infuriate William.

He told the Press Association, "In the short term, Harry will be able to deepen his rapprochement with his father. And his presence back home will make it harder for his brother to duck a reconciliation. The surprise return of Harry and Meghan is likely to have left William apoplectic."

What are Harry and Meghan doing in the U.K.?

A source close to the Sussexes told AP that Harry will be able to devote more time to his charitable work in Britain, while Meghan will continue running her lifestyle business, As Ever, from the U.K.

Meghan may also return to acting, with Australian news outlet News.com.au reporting that one reason for the couple's decision to relocate to Britain was that Meghan had been offered a role in an upcoming project. A source close to the duchess did not deny the report.

Deadline reported that Meghan has had preliminary conversations about a potential role in the Netflix series The Gentlemen , which would mark her first significant acting role since her marriage to Harry in 2018.

The couple has been based in Montecito since moving to California after stepping away from royal duties in 2020.

The Telegraph reported that Harry wanted a "refuge" in the U.K. and the "freedom to enjoy British summers, see friends and come and go without the 'circus' that has surrounded recent visits."

During their years in the U.S., Harry and Meghan signed deals with Netflix and Spotify and spoke publicly about their experiences within the royal family. Harry published his memoir, Spare , which became a bestseller. Their Spotify partnership later ended, while Reuters reported that Meghan's Netflix lifestyle show was not renewed for a third season.

Harry has also spent years pursuing legal cases in Britain, including disputes involving the British press and a challenge over the level of police protection available to him and his family when they visit the country.

articles.title: Patricia Pardo se disculpa por sus palabras acerca de los migrantes que sostuvieron la cría de delfín: “Me confundí”
articles.standfirst: La presentadora ha denunciado que ha recibido amenazas de muerte contra sus tres hijos
articles.summary: La presentadora ha denunciado que ha recibido amenazas de muerte contra sus tres hijos
articles.body: La presentadora del programa ‘Vamos a Ver’ de Telecinco, Patricia Pardo, ha dedicado este lunes, 7 de septiembre, un espacio en su programa para pedir disculpas por sus palabras acerca de los migrantes que capturaron y sostuvieron una cría de delfín en Ceuta. Pardo ha salido durante la última emisión de su programa a disculparse por sus declaraciones del pasado viernes, después de que el caso de la cría de delfín que levantaron unos migrantes generase una indignación generalizada en todo el país. Ante esta situación, la presentadora, lejos de denunciar el maltrato sufrido por el animal, le restó importancia a la situación alegando que existían problemas más graves. Este lunes Pardo ha rectificado sus palabras y ha confesado que no estuvo acertada: “Quiero pedirles perdón y rectificar parte de mi discurso del viernes. Me confundí porque tendría que haber empezado condenando de manera enérgica y contundente la escena terrorífica de la cría de delfín. No lo hice. Opté por otra explicación. Me confundí” Además, Patricia ha argumentado que su discurso generó en la opinión pública un malentendido sobre su posicionamiento respecto al maltrato animal: “Lo que hice con esto es que muchos de ustedes pensaran que a mí me da exactamente igual que alguien maltrate, agreda o mate a una cría de delfín. Ni mucho menos". Por otro lado, explica que no emitió las imágenes de la situación porque no quería contribuir a generar más polarización. “Yo no quería dar esas imágenes porque creo que nosotros tenemos una grandísima responsabilidad. Creo que, quizá, esas imágenes, descontextualizadas o utilizadas no hacen más que cooperar a aumentar esa polarización, esa deshumanización y esa instrumentalización del inmigrante”, sostiene Pardo. Por último, la presentadora también ha aprovechado para denunciar que tanto ella como sus hijos han recibido amenazas de muerte que son del todo inaceptables: “Este fin de semana he reflexionado mucho, he recibido unas críticas feroces. No hay derecho a recibir amenazas de muerte a tres niños pequeños que son mis hijos. Creo que ya está bien”.

articles.summary: El reputado cocinero cree que esta receta es perfecta para acompañar cualquier elaboración
articles.body: El final del verano comienza a acercarse, así que hay que aprovechar hasta el último día para elaborar nuestras recetas favoritas de esta parte del año. Más allá de los clásicos, Jordi Cruz ha compartido en sus redes sociales un clásico oriental que se puede convertir en uno de los preferidos en casa. Esta elaboración es perfecta para acompañar cualquier plato. Desconocido para muchos, el chef nos descubre los secretos mejor guardados del Baba Ganoush. “Es uno de los grandes clásicos de Oriente Medio. Un puré de berenjena ahumada, cremoso y lleno de sabor, perfecto para acompañar con pan de pita, totopos o cualquier pan plano”, asegura el también jurado de ‘MasterChef’, de RTVE. Para aquellos que no sabían de su existencia, el reputado chef desvela cuál es el origen de este plato y de su nombre: “Baba Ganoush suele traducirse como ‘papá mimado’ o ‘papá consentido’ y es una receta tradicional presente en numerosos países de Oriente Medio”. Si tuviese que definirlo con una palabra, Cruz lo haría con lo mejor que se puede decir de una receta: “Está riquísimo”. Para elaborar la receta, Jordi Cruz recomienda dividirla en cuatro sencillos pasos. En primer lugar, preparar las berenjenas: córtalas por la mitad y cúbrelas con sal gruesa durante aproximadamente 1 hora para reducir su amargor. Después, acláralas con agua. También es importante darles un toque ahumado: tuesta la piel directamente sobre una parrilla o llama hasta que quede oscura. Más tarde, envuelve las berenjenas en papel de aluminio y hornéalas a 180 °C durante 25-30 minutos, hasta que estén tiernas. Por último, la clave está en extraer la pulpa y combinarla con el ajo: retira la piel con una cuchara, guarda los jugos que hayan soltado durante la cocción y mézclala con el ajo, el zumo de limón y el tahini. Tritura hasta conseguir una crema fina y homogénea y ajusta la sal al gusto.

articles.body: The Matrix was said to be coming back for a fifth time back in 2024, with director Drew Goddard at the helm. We haven’t heard much since then, until Matrix co-creator and co-director Lilly Wachowski told KCRW last week that Goddard was waiting on the Wachowski sisters’ blessing to move forward. Lilly seems over the whole affair, saying that she “doesn’t want to play in that sandbox anymore.” Here’s the rest of what she said about moving forward for Matrix 5: > He doesn’t wanna go forward unless he gets our blessing, and so, it becomes this complicated situation that maybe we’re gonna stick our noses in a tiny bit and see how we feel and if we wanna pass on our blessing to Drew or not.
